title: Anchored dual-rate + auto-adjusting session credits probe
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Objective: validate a hybrid pricing probe that (1) charges distinct ingress/output per-token rates anchored to a baseline, and (2) dynamically issues and reclaims short-lived session credits to smooth billing for short bursty users. Hypothesis: Combining a modest output premium with automatic session crediting will reduce invoice volatility for heavy-chat customers while preserving unit economics for steady-throughput ML workloads. Success metrics: lower weekly invoice variance for cohort A vs control, <5% uplift in per-token revenue for equivalent latency workloads, no significant increase in charge disputes in first 30 days.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Experiment runs with two cohorts (control: current symmetric rate; test: anchored dual-rate + auto credits) for 30 days across ~50 accounts.
2) Telemetry pipelines show ingress/egress token breakdown and session credit churn by account.
3) Billing UI surfaces session credit usage and remaining auto-credits per account.
4) Cost model simulation shows expected unit margin >= baseline on 90th percentile workload.
5) Legal/Finance sign-off on terms and dashboard wording; security SQ completed if required.

notes: Key trade-offs: automatic credits reduce short-term dispute noise but add accounting complexity and subtle incentives (users may split sessions to maximize credits). Mitigations: short TTL on credits, per-account rate-limits on auto-credit issuance, clear UI communication. Follow-up tickets expected: PM-920011 (session-credit TTL policy), ENG-20345 (billing audit events), DES-4021 (credit UX microcopy).
